topics.title: CSS Variables (Custom Properties)
topics.summary: Define reusable values with --name and read them with var() - they cascade and inherit.
keyPoints: Declare with --name, read with var(--name, fallback)
:root holds global tokens
They inherit and can be overridden in any scope
They can be changed at runtime with JavaScript
Cannot be used inside media query conditions
pitfalls: Typos in variable names produce silent failures
Putting spaces or units wrong: --gap: 8 then var(--gap)px does not work (use calc())
Expecting Sass-style compile-time calculation

interview.q: What are CSS variables and how do you declare them?
interview.a: Custom properties declared with a -- prefix (e.g. --main-color: #3498db) and read with var(--main-color).

interview.q: How do CSS variables differ from Sass variables?
interview.a: CSS variables exist at runtime, cascade/inherit, can be changed by JS and media queries; Sass variables are compiled away.

interview.q: How do you provide a fallback value?
interview.a: var(--color, #333) - the second argument is used if the variable is not defined.

Expose component knobs as local custom properties
calc(var(--x) * unit) to scale values

interview.q: What is @property?
interview.a: An at-rule that registers a custom property with a syntax type, initial value and inheritance, enabling validation and smooth animation.

interview.q: How do you build a theme switcher with variables?
interview.a: Define tokens on :root and override them under [data-theme="dark"] or a class; toggle the attribute with JavaScript.

interview.q: How can you use a unitless custom property as a length?
interview.a: Multiply it inside calc(): calc(var(--n) * 1px).

topics.title: Cascade Layers (@layer)
topics.summary: Control which group of styles wins with explicit layers instead of specificity wars.
keyPoints: Declare order: @layer reset, base, components, utilities;
Later layer wins regardless of specificity
Unlayered styles beat layered styles
!important reverses the layer order
Great for taming third-party CSS
pitfalls: Forgetting that unlayered CSS always wins
Declaring layer order too late (the first appearance decides)
Assuming high specificity helps inside a lower layer

examples.title: Layer order beats specificity
examples.explanation: The button is crimson even though the component rule uses an id plus class.

interview.q: What problem do cascade layers solve?
interview.a: They let you define explicit priority between groups of styles so specificity wars and !important are not needed, especially with third-party CSS.

interview.q: Do unlayered styles beat layered styles?
interview.a: Yes. Styles outside any layer take precedence over layered styles (for normal declarations).

interview.q: How does !important behave with layers?
interview.a: The order reverses: !important in an earlier layer beats !important in a later layer.

topics.title: Logical Properties and Writing Modes
topics.summary: Use inline/block instead of left/right/top/bottom so layouts adapt to any writing direction.
topics.description:
Physical properties (`left`, `margin-top`, `width`) assume left-to-right, top-to-bottom text. **Logical properties** map to the **inline** axis (the direction text flows) and **block** axis (where new lines stack), so layouts work for RTL languages (Arabic, Hebrew) and vertical scripts.

### Mapping (horizontal-tb, LTR)
| Physical | Logical |
|---|---|
| `width` / `height` | `inline-size` / `block-size` |
| `margin-left` / `margin-right` | `margin-inline-start` / `margin-inline-end` |
| `margin-top` / `margin-bottom` | `margin-block-start` / `margin-block-end` |
| `padding: 0 1rem` | `padding-inline: 1rem` |
| `border-top` + `border-bottom` | `border-block` |
| `left` / `top` | `inset-inline-start` / `inset-block-start` |
| `text-align: left` | `text-align: start` |
| `top/right/bottom/left: 0` | `inset: 0` |

### Shorthands
`margin-inline`, `margin-block`, `padding-inline`, `padding-block`, `border-inline`, `border-block`, `inset-inline`, `inset-block`.

### writing-mode
`writing-mode: horizontal-tb | vertical-rl | vertical-lr;` rotates the flow of text. In vertical mode, `inline-size` becomes the height! (The source demo used `writing-mode: vertical-lr` on a heading.)

### Practical use
```css
.container { max-inline-size: 70ch; margin-inline: auto; padding-block: 2rem; }
.icon + .label { margin-inline-start: .5rem; }  /* flips automatically in RTL */
```

### Tip
Set `dir="rtl"` or `html { direction: rtl }` to test; logical code mirrors itself with no extra CSS.
keyPoints: inline axis = text direction; block axis = line stacking
margin-inline / padding-block etc. replace left/right/top/bottom
inset: 0 replaces top/right/bottom/left: 0
text-align: start/end adapts to direction
writing-mode changes the flow and swaps axes
pitfalls: Mixing physical and logical properties inconsistently
Forgetting that in vertical writing modes inline-size is height
Assuming margin-left: auto will flip in RTL (it will not)

interview.q: What are logical properties?
interview.a: Properties like margin-inline-start or inline-size that are relative to the writing direction (inline/block axes) instead of physical left/right/top/bottom.

interview.q: Why use margin-inline: auto instead of margin: 0 auto?
interview.a: It is equivalent in LTR but expresses intent on the inline axis and adapts to vertical writing modes; both center a block.

interview.q: What does the writing-mode property do?
interview.a: It sets whether lines of text are laid out horizontally or vertically and the direction blocks progress.

interview.q: How do you add a custom font in CSS?
interview.a: Use @font-face with a font-family name and src url(); then reference the family in font-family with fallbacks.

interview.q: What does font-display: swap do?
interview.a: It renders text immediately with a fallback font and swaps to the custom font when it has loaded, preventing invisible text.

interview.q: What is a variable font?
interview.a: A single font file containing continuous design axes (weight, width, slant) so you can choose any value in the range with font-weight or font-variation-settings.

topics.title: Scroll Snap and Smooth Scrolling
topics.summary: Make carousels and full-page sections lock into place with scroll-snap and smooth behavior.
topics.description:
**Scroll snap** makes a scroll container stop at defined positions - ideal for carousels, galleries and slide-style pages, with no JavaScript.

### Container
```css
.scroller {
  display: flex;
  overflow-x: auto;
  scroll-snap-type: x mandatory;   /* axis + strictness */
  scroll-behavior: smooth;
  gap: 1rem;
}
```
- `scroll-snap-type: x | y | both` + `mandatory` or `proximity`.
- `mandatory` always settles on a snap point; `proximity` only if close.

### Items
```css
.slide { flex: 0 0 100%; scroll-snap-align: center; }  /* start | center | end */
```
- `scroll-snap-stop: always;` prevents skipping items on fast swipes.

### Offsets
- `scroll-padding` on the container and `scroll-margin` on items - essential when you have a sticky header.

### Smooth anchor scrolling
```css
html { scroll-behavior: smooth; scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
```
The final project in the course left `scroll-snap-type: y proximity` and `scroll-snap-align: center` commented in its stylesheet - it is exactly this feature applied page-wide.

### Notes
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for smooth scrolling.
- Hide scrollbars carefully (`scrollbar-width: none`) - keep navigation dots/arrows for accessibility.
- Use `overscroll-behavior` to stop scroll chaining.
- Newer: `scroll-timeline` / scroll-driven animations tie animation progress to scrolling.
keyPoints: scroll-snap-type on the container, scroll-snap-align on children
mandatory always snaps; proximity snaps when near
scroll-padding/margin account for sticky headers
scroll-behavior: smooth animates anchor jumps
Carousels without JavaScript
pitfalls: mandatory snapping with items taller than the viewport (trapped scrolling)
Forgetting scroll-padding with a fixed header
Hiding scroll UI without providing other controls

interview.q: How do you build a carousel without JavaScript?
interview.a: A horizontally scrolling flex container with scroll-snap-type: x mandatory and children with scroll-snap-align: center (plus overflow-x: auto).

interview.q: mandatory vs proximity?
interview.a: mandatory forces the scroll to rest on a snap point; proximity only snaps if the scroll stops near one.

interview.q: How do you offset snapping/anchor scroll below a sticky header?
interview.a: Use scroll-padding-top on the scroll container or scroll-margin-top on the targets.

interview.q: What problem does subgrid solve?
interview.a: It lets nested grid items align to the parent grid's tracks, e.g. keeping titles, text and buttons aligned across cards of different content length.

interview.q: How do you use subgrid?
interview.a: On a grid item that spans tracks, set display: grid and grid-template-rows/columns: subgrid.

interview.q: Does subgrid inherit gap?
interview.a: Yes by default it uses the parent's gap, which can be overridden on the subgrid.

topics.title: Dark Mode and prefers-color-scheme
topics.summary: Respect the OS theme with prefers-color-scheme and build a manual toggle with variables.
topics.description:
Dark mode is mostly a **color-token** problem. Define colors as custom properties and swap them.

### 1. Automatic: follow the system
```css
:root { --bg: #ffffff; --text: #0f172a; --card: #f1f5f9; color-scheme: light dark; }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root { --bg: #0b1020; --text: #e2e8f0; --card: #1e293b; }
}
body { background: var(--bg); color: var(--text); }
```

- `color-scheme: light dark;` lets the browser render built-in widgets (scrollbars, form controls) in the right theme.
- The modern `light-dark()` function: `color: light-dark(#111, #eee);`

### 2. Manual toggle (user choice)
```css
:root[data-theme="dark"] { --bg: #0b1020; --text: #e2e8f0; }
```
Toggle `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` with JavaScript and save to `localStorage`. Read the system value first with `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')`.

### 3. Design tips
- Do not use pure black (#000) on pure white - choose dark gray (#0b1020, #121212).
- Reduce saturation of accent colors in dark mode.
- Use elevation (lighter surface) instead of heavy shadows.
- Check contrast again for both themes.
- Dim images: `img { filter: brightness(.9); }`.

### Avoid flash
Set the theme attribute in an inline script **before** the stylesheet paints.
keyPoints: Use custom properties for colors and swap them in a media query
prefers-color-scheme reads the OS preference
color-scheme: light dark styles native controls
Manual toggle via data-theme + localStorage
Re-check contrast and avoid pure black
pitfalls: Hard-coded colors scattered in components
Flash of wrong theme before JavaScript runs
Forgetting images, shadows and form controls in dark mode

interview.q: How do you detect dark mode in CSS?
interview.a: @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { ... } reflects the user's operating system or browser preference.

interview.q: What does color-scheme: light dark do?
interview.a: It tells the browser the page supports both schemes so built-in UI like form controls and scrollbars are drawn with the matching theme.

interview.q: How do you let users override the system theme?
interview.a: Use a data-theme attribute (or class) on the root with variable overrides, toggle it with JavaScript and persist the choice in localStorage.
